concern_details.detail: required runtime environments and software artifacts
concern_details.why: Java 23 JVM, the application jar, the dependency jars with versions matching pom.xml (hibernate-core 6.6.50.Final, mysql-connector-j 9.4.0, forms_rt 7.0.3), persistence.xml and the MySQL server are all shown, and the diagram says the MySQL version is not specified. The launch note covers the missing Main-Class and the classpath launch. Small gaps: Maven is a build-time requirement (README 'Requirements'), and the dependency box lists only direct dependencies, not that Hibernate brings transitive jars (jakarta.persistence-api etc.) that must also be on the classpath.

concern_details.detail: where the application runs and where its data is stored
concern_details.why: Both the Swing client JVM and MySQL are on one workstation, which matches the JDBC URL jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:3306/reports_db and the 'reports_user'@'localhost' grant. Data is in schema reports_db inside the MySQL execution environment.

concern_details.detail: how the main runtime elements communicate
concern_details.why: A single communication path, JDBC over TCP :3306 on loopback, between the JVM and MySQL. The code has no other runtime link (no server tier, no network API).

concern_details.detail: technologies and runtime dependencies between the application and the database
concern_details.why: Hibernate/JPA (persistence unit loaded in JpaUtil), the Connector/J driver (com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver), credentials hard-coded in persistence.xml, hbm2ddl.auto=update, and the manual CREATE DATABASE/USER/GRANT steps are all given. The note also says a remote host means editing the config, rebuilding and changing the grant.

level_why: Seven elements: one device, two execution environments and four artifacts, with versions, port, protocol, launch and DB preparation. That is what a DevOps engineer needs to stand the system up. Application layers are rightly left out, and the three library jars are rightly merged into one artifact.
missing: Maven as the build tool needed to produce the jar (README 'Requirements: Java 23, Maven, MySQL'). Today it appears only in the README. It could go in the launch note.
Hibernate's transitive dependencies must also be on the runtime classpath. The 'dependency jars' artifact names only the three direct dependencies from pom.xml.
uml: persistence.xml is drawn as a separate artifact deployed in the JVM, next to the jar. It is packaged inside the jar (src/main/resources/META-INF). In UML it should be nested in the jar artifact, or shown as a <<deploymentSpec>> attached to the jar, so that it does not look like a separately deployed file. The label says 'packaged in jar', but the notation contradicts it.
The app-to-persistence.xml <<use>> dependency is redundant once persistence.xml is nested in the jar or modelled as its deployment specification.
fixes: Nest persistence.xml inside the jar artifact, or model it as a <<deploymentSpec>> of the jar, and drop the separate <<use>> arrow to it.
Add Maven (build-time) to the launch note, and say that Hibernate's transitive jars are also needed on the classpath (for example via mvn dependency:copy-dependencies).
